Visit note | 2026-01-04 11:00 AM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Tamim Howlader, 51, male. Mr. Howlader attends for review regarding his ongoing condition. He reports that he has been losing weight steadily despite eating well, alongside noticing bothersome shaky hands and a racing pulse. He works as a journalist and mentioned these issues became prominent during a hot summer in Khulna. He has a known history of Bronchial asthma, for which he uses regular inhalers. He denies any chest pain, visual changes, or significant weakness in his limbs. On examination today: pulse 113 bpm, BP 116/76 mmHg, weight 61 kg. Neck examination reveals a diffuse, soft, non-tender enlargement of the thyroid gland without palpable nodules or bruits. Chest auscultation reveals clear breath sounds with no wheeze. Assessment: Hyperthyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued for his condition. He was advised to avoid excess tea and coffee, and to rest whenever his heart races.
